newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan told of Britain's support for U.N. reform.
newsitem.headline: Annan told of Britain's support for U.N. reform.

text.p: Britain has drawn the attention of Secretary-General Kofi Annan to a statement by Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind supporting U.N. reforms and stressing the need for members to pay their dues.

Rifkind's statement, made in answer to a recent question in the House of Commons, was enclosed with a letter that British U.N. ambassador Sir John Weston sent to the secretary-general over the weekend.

"When he (Annan) visited London last month the Prime Minister and I were impressed by his determination to give reform a high priority. We support him in his determination to secure tighter budgeting, greater management efficiency and the elimination of overlap between different U.N. bodies," Rifkind said.
But he said the United Nations needed not only to reform itself but to be able to rely on the financial resources U.N. members had voted.

Rifkind said he raised "our concerns on this score" with U.S. congressmen when he visited Washington earlier this month, noting U.S. arrears of $1.3 billion at the end of 1996 represented approximately two-thirds of total U.N. arrears.

One of the effects of the backlog, he noted, was that countries contributing to U.N. peacekeeping operations, such as India, Bangladesh and Britain, did not get paid what they were owed. In Britain's case this now amounted to 40 million pounds sterling (about $64 million).

"I made it clear in Washington that this failure to honor financial obligations under the U.N. Charter does the cause of U.N. reform no good and causes resentment among friends and allies. I know that President (Bill) Clinton is committed to solving this problem," Rifkind added.
He called for a new and fairer system of U.N. financing based more closely on the capacity to pay and on assurances that all members would in future pay fully, unconditionally and on time.

"Once the problem of arrears has been dealt with, the British government hopes it will be possible speedily to complete the process of U.N. reform and thus to relaunch the United Nations on its urgent new agenda," Rifkind added.
